detail.longDescription: I wanted to share evalkit - an open source framework for improving agents that we built. https://evalkit.inferedge.com/ Like most people, we used phoenix, langfuse, but these are good recording traces, managing datasets etc. But the process around evals, agent improvements, regressions, mapping errors/failures to code or prompts has to be hand rolled. We still use self-hosted phoenix, but mainly as a database. Our process was trace mining, converting them into evals, getting them reviewed by an expert, and then re-running datasets to create baseline scores or internal benchmarks for our agents. We found other companies also follow similar processes in-house, but there is no good framework to do everything e2e. So we carved out what we built into evalkit. - evalkit automatically groups similar traces into one issue bucket (similar to how one issue in sentry can link to multiple events) - Expert review workflow with simple english rubrics (instead of json) - Coding agent first approach - we expect your coding agent to be able to do most steps, and you rarely have to open the UI An example of how we used it in-house: evalkit identified 89 traces in on bucket, suggested 14 cases, which resulted in 4 merged PRs. We saw 90% reduction in failures, 80% reduction in token consumption (and cost), and 45% in time. This is pretty early, and we are adding features every few days. If you feel this is useful, or have any suggestions, reach out to us on evalkit@inferedge.com or join our slack community and give us some love by starring us on github :)
